title: Book of Proof
note: Solutions to odd-numbered exercises (PDF pp. 304–375) are not broken down. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A transition-to-proofs textbook that teaches how to read and write mathematical proofs. It starts with sets, logic and counting, then covers the standard techniques for conditional statements (direct, contrapositive, contradiction), other kinds of statements (if-and-only-if, existence, uniqueness), proofs about sets, disproof by counterexample and mathematical induction, and finally relations, functions, a chapter of ε–δ proofs in calculus, and cardinality of sets including Cantor’s theorem.
